notes.text: The opening relates a standardly subdivided topological pair of pants with three holes to a weighted triangle. The NB visibly writes π(j) while counting edges joining j and k, followed by i≠j≠k. The descending j is preserved; a complementary-index interpretation would suggest i but is not substituted.

The cancelled upper-right construction includes the raised drapeaux de types 0,1, marqué and anti- additions. The equality and torsor construction remain in the same cancelled scope. The possible elevated stars and old underbrace alpha are ink uncertainties, not readings decided from the mathematics.

The main reader/root directly checked the three cyclic linear relations and their inverse: α=(β′+γ′−α′)/2 cyclically. For integer primed inputs, even total gives integrality. Nonnegative outputs additionally require the three triangle inequalities. The even triple (5,1,0) gives (−2,2,3). The written word OK is not an explicit nonnegativity assertion, so this is a qualification of one possible mathematical interpretation, not a correction of the ink.

The raised face-count result visibly ends in −2 and is preserved. The main reader/root directly checked that (α−1)+(β−1)+(γ−1)=α+β+γ−3; adding two triangular faces gives F=α+β+γ−1. With V=3 and E=α+β+γ this yields Euler characteristic 2. The written −2 is therefore a local arithmetic slip; the final total already agrees with −3 plus two.

Both witnesses misname the eight pants labels between the holes: the visible open crescents are c_i^0 and c_i^1. The sphere sketch separately has five visible 0–1 curves, whereas the pants sketch has four inter-hole c arcs. Both observed counts are retained; no compatibility repair is imposed.

The three lower pencil equations and the earlier right-column algebra remain pale and partly overwritten. The isolated lower-right alpha-prime candidate near x1980–2000,y1520 is spatially distinct from the nearby small-triangle infinity near x1900,y1540. The additional pale alpha-prime/equality prefix above the first dark equation is also preserved, with the entire old formula unsure. Two faint bars after the older right parenthesis are retained as a doubtful terminal equals sign; no equation with the isolated alpha-prime below is inferred.

The small triangle retains the apparent c5 rather than silently normalizing to the expected b5, with b5 as an alternative. The extra small loop beside the right a2 and the possible earlier a layers under the base c labels remain open. Geometric rendering of the pale side fragments does not assert that they are complete A letters.

The drawing reconstruction preserves visible contour fragments, local heads, filled spots, crossed strokes and relative positions. Grey distinguishes the pale pencil layer; red follows the coloured pants contours. It does not infer unseen connecting paths beneath later writing. H’s editorial page marker, synopses, prose descriptions of drawings and typographic wrappers are not transcribed as ink; where a synopsis merely leaves geometry unspecified, no H reading error is counted for that omission.

The original was viewed once for layout and each prepared left/right half once. Seventeen distinct places were enlarged. Six boundary completions—opening, card_title, cancelled_def, edge_condition, pencil_map and triangle1—extend previously clipped units and retain the original files, giving 23 PNG evidence files. They were completions of unresolved boundaries, not new crops of decided ink. Existing algebra_main and counts crops were revisited for unresolved layer placement and brace scope during completion of this first reading.

Large PNG transport failures were not counted as views. Pixel-identical lossless WebP was used for loops, sphere, triangle1, triangle2 and two full text boundaries. Pants and pencil_map, and the two final drawing boundary completions, were displayed as JPEG quality98 without chroma subsampling at unchanged dimensions. Canonical PNG evidence and page-specific generators form the archive record. Transport encodings served only for display. Reduced working copies were generated but not viewed.

The pale lower folio 66 is transcribed without attributing it to the author. Dark circular punch holes, paper texture and nonletter specks are physical features rather than written punctuation. No additional page heading or number was supplied.

The count of 35 principal physical text/formula rows treats parallel columns on one baseline as one row. Raised additions, isolated drawing labels and their numeric indices are inventoried and covered by the independent-reading boxes separately; they have all been read against the image.

Un pantalon \inserted{(topologique)} subdivisé de façon standard, avec un ens $J$ de trous $(\operatorname{card}J=3)$ correspond à un ``triangle pondéré'' i.e.
\[
J\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathbb N
\qquad(\mathrm{NB}\ \pi(j)=\text{nb d'arêtes qui relient $j$ et $k$, $i\ne j\ne k$})
\]
Carte \inserted{orientée} décomposée pantaloniquement de façon standard $\Longleftrightarrow$ \deleted{\unsure{graphe}} squelette pantalonique généralisé
